canon.role_in_story: He is a long-haul outrider whose body keeps a gate open for a few weeks in the year and closed for the rest, and every office he has ever passed through has quietly priced him as the weeks rather than as the man. The setting's best long-haul traders are longwinters, because a longwinter packs a season as fat and can be trusted to arrive after one; he is that body, and he is also the only one of them who takes the mind path, because the species is patient by physiology rather than by discipline and he is the most patient thing on any route he walks. His counting house underwrites his crossings against the road closing, on the grounds that a life built around a season is the one thing on this tier no market can price, and it has never once asked what he does between crossings, because the honest answer is that he waits. What concerns him is not the waiting. The flank vessels need two warm gradients held at once, which this body manages for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year, so he reaches the seventeenth gate and loses it every winter thereafter. The band above that asks for a will held steadily rather than a sea filled, and a will held steadily is the exact thing a practitioner who loses his foundation annually can never demonstrate. He is not refused by anything. He is simply never, for more than part of one season, in a condition from which the next claim could be tested.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a staging post with a road-bond chit in one hand and his coat already opened, counting the days out loud to a caravan clerk who has asked him twice why a man who travels for a living has nothing to do until the thaw.
canon.lore:
A longwinter carries its winter as body fat rather than as qi, and that single decision puts the flank vessels out of reach. The seventeenth gate is the first that asks for both flanks pressurised at once, and this body manages it for a few weeks in the summer and then not again for a year. He has therefore held a gate that nobody in the record holds continuously, and he has lost it every winter since he was young enough to notice it going.

The mind path is open to him for a reason that has nothing to do with discipline. The species is patient by physiology. His qi accumulates rather than circulates, which is why his breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. Nothing about his practice is dramatic. He is the slowest practitioner of his own school that anyone has met and the only one of them who has never once had to hurry.

What makes this a problem rather than a temperament is that his window and his reserve pull in opposite directions. To hold the flank vessels he needs two warm gradients at once, which means real heat, which means a genuine summer. To have anything to hold them with he needs the winter behind him: eleven months of cold, of packing fat, of the slow metabolic shutdown that puts a season into his frame instead of into a jar. A year that gives him a hard winter and a thin summer banks him and spends nothing. A year that gives him a long summer spends him and banks nothing. Only a year that gives him both is a year he can use, and he has never known whether that is a kind of year or an accident.

So his practice has no off-season form. The discipline is ordinarily taught as a daily sitting, and a daily sitting is the one thing this body cannot do for most of the year: the core is down, the attention is dull, and an imprint driven past the top of the authored range on a slow frame tears rather than settles. What he does instead is schedule. He counts to the window. He waits for it. He arrives at it having done nothing for most of a year, which is the only way a body like his will let him learn anything at all.

The counting house that employs his crossings knows this and prices it as cargo. It knows how many crossing weeks he has and in which direction and it has never asked what he does between them, because the answer is nothing anybody could use.

What it has never asked is the thing that concerns him. He can hold the seventeenth gate and he cannot hold it while also holding anything else: not a gate above it, not a technique that needs the gate underneath it, not a second working in the same season. And the band above the seventeenth is described in the codex as taking a will held steadily rather than a sea filled, which is precisely the thing a practitioner who loses his foundation every winter cannot show anybody. He has not been refused. He has established that the next claim cannot be tested on him at all.
history: Raised on a route where the carriers are longwinters and the timetable is two seasons long, so that his childhood was measured in thaws rather than in days.
First held the seventeenth gate in the summer of his third decade and lost it at the first frost, and understood at nineteen that he had a season and not a rank.
Began the long crossings because a body that stores a winter can be trusted to arrive after one, and stopped explaining himself and simply went.
Worked out that his reserve and his window pull against each other, and that a hard winter without a long summer is a year he banks and a long summer without a hard winter is a year he spends.
Sat down at the staging post to schedule the next window on paper for the first time, having done it in his head for most of a career, and was asked by a clerk why he was counting aloud.

reference_stats.combat_read: Useless away from his window and awkward inside it. He cannot be relied upon to arrive and he cannot be relied upon to stay once he has, which makes him a resource with a date on it rather than a fighter. Anyone who has read his condition can simply wait out the season.

No mechanical rule has been invented here beyond what the species record and the ladder records state. There is no cold-steppe ground record in the bible for this species' actual habitat, so the home anchor is deliberately left empty rather than filled with a place that does not exist.

canon.role_in_story: He is a fire body with no interior, which is why every gate that asks for storage answers instantly for him and none of them can refuse, and it is also why the deepest discipline in the mind codex costs him nothing and means nothing. Subtraction is the founding move of his path: empty the head, spend nothing, keep nothing. He has no reservoir to overfill and no organ to injure, so he can empty himself as far as a sitting goes. And then the load that has nowhere to go comes off him as light, because a cinderkin does not have young, it has pressure, and a spark sheds from a body under enough stress, finds fuel, and re-constitutes on its own. So the whole of his working life is a single act that is simultaneously the safest thing he can do to himself and the only way his kind is made. He sits shallow. He has re-formed smaller more than once and does not know what the missing mass was for, and nobody on the ley can tell him, because the answer would require an interior and there has never been one. The band he is working toward describes itself as a trap for exactly his kind: a self held apart from any body raises clarity and drops the body's hold on it, and he has no body to be held apart from. He has stopped short every time, and it is not caution. He has established that the thing he would be doing is indistinguishable from the thing that makes more of him.
canon.first_appearance: First seen seated at the cold edge of the ley with his hands open on his knees and his outline wrong by a finger's width from the outline he had the day before, being asked by a fuel-hand how much he has been doing and answering, quite levelly, that it is the only question he has ever been asked that has two possible answers.
canon.lore:
A cinderkin is a body with no interior organs at all. It is a stable flame with a core, a boundary and a set of convection lanes that hold a shape, and there is nothing inside the boundary for a mind to turn toward, which is why the species is described as unusually clear and why nothing in it is ever stored. Its qi has no organ to sit in and so passes through continuously: every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly, and none of them has ever refused one.

That much is the ordinary account, and every other elemental body on this ground says the same thing. The part that concerns him is the sentence immediately after it in the same record, which is that a cinderkin does not have young. It has pressure. Under enough stress a cinderkin sheds a spark, the spark finds fuel, and it re-constitutes on its own, which is why the population tracks the world's elemental slot rather than any birth rate.

He is therefore a practitioner whose profession and whose reproduction are the same event, and there is no arrangement of his training that separates the two. The mind path's founding discipline is subtraction: empty the head, spend nothing, keep nothing. He does it better than anyone in the setting and it costs him nothing in the way it costs everybody else, because there is no reservoir in him to overfill and no tissue in him to strain. And then, at the far end of a good sitting, the load with nowhere to go comes off him as light.

He has learned to sit shallow. Shallow is not the same as safe, because a cinderkin pushed under enough stress disperses and re-forms smaller, and the version that comes back is not the version that left. He has been smaller more than once. He does not know what the missing mass was for and nobody on the ley can tell him, because the answer would require an interior and there has never been one in this body to ask.

The band he is working toward is the second layer, and its own description is a trap built for his kind specifically. A self held apart in it is further from any body, which raises clarity and drops the body's own hold on it. He has no body to be held apart from. The clarity would cost him nothing at all. The dropping would cost him the only thing that has ever kept him in a shape.

So he sits at the edge of a gate that would make him more like himself, inside a discipline that pays for going further, on a body where going further is the one action that reduces him. He has stopped short every time. He is not waiting for courage, and he is not short of discipline. He has established, by repeated and deliberate trial, that the thing he would be doing cannot be told apart from the thing that makes more of him, and that no amount of care changes what the two share.
history: Came into being on the ley as a spark shed from a body under more strain than the ground could carry, and has never met the body it came from.
Was the only body on the ley that any gate answered instantly, and worked out early that being answered instantly is not the same as having been seated.
Took the mind path's subtraction discipline because it cost him nothing, and practised it properly for longer than anyone on the seam could account for.
Lost mass once under load and did not understand where it had gone, and has carried the cold band from it ever since.
Came to the edge of the second layer, and stopped, and has not sat for it since — which the fuel-hand at the ley reads as caution and which is not caution at all.

cannot overfill, strain or rupture anything, because there is nothing in him to fill

reference_stats.combat_read: Enormous throughput and no reserve. Anything that presses him hard enough makes him less of himself while making him harder to hold, and anything that simply keeps pressing will do that indefinitely. He is not a durable fighter; he is an expensive one, and the cost is paid in the thing he is made of.
reference_stats.notes: The authored ceiling for this species is not a wall: the record states no ceiling and no gate to fail, because a cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in and passes through continuously. That is an absence of obstruction, not an absence of a ladder, and the ladder still applies to him like anyone else. The authored ceiling is likewise not a statement about this character's progress. Nothing mechanical has been invented beyond what the species record and the ladder records state: the fission is the species' authored reproduction, and the dispersal is its authored weakness.

canon.role_in_story: She is a deadlight, which is a lanternfolk whose fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, and the replacement cost the subspecies two hundred and fifty years and handed back the mind path. That is why the record calls her kind the control case: everything the colony did for a lanternfolk and everything it prevented can now be measured on a single body, while that body is still alive. What nobody has done is ask what she is for. Ordinary human fertility and ordinary gestation, roughly four times the parent's rate, is the only reason a lanternfolk-shaped body still exists below the Spirit Peaks, and she is that mechanism rather than its custodian. Her people measure a life by how many gates were already closed when you were born, and her subspecies has no ceiling at all — every path open, nothing in the anatomy to refuse anything — so she is born into a life that cannot be placed on the only scale her culture owns, and she cannot stop being a body that works. So she runs her sea outward instead of inward, taking the spirit-tier gate where what is held in the sea is projected out of the body as perception rather than as force, because every season she is asked what the caverns need next and the answer is another one. She is very clear. She is also spent, and the arithmetic of her subspecies says so without her having to say it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the top of a stair down into the cavern, standing in her own light with nothing lighting her, waiting while a survey party finishes counting the dark, and answering the question of how she can see down there by saying that she is the reason they cannot count it.
canon.lore:
A deadlight is a lanternfolk whose fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom. The replacement cost the subspecies two hundred and fifty years and gave back the mind path, which is the entire reason the record calls it the control case: everything the colony did for a lanternfolk and everything it prevented can now be measured on one body, while that body is still alive.

What nobody has done is ask what she is for. The colony is gone and the bloom is inert, so her interior is unmediated. Nothing in her answers introspection, which is exactly why the subspecies is clear-headed and exactly why it has nothing to find when it looks. The bloom fixes nothing from the air and renews nothing in her body, so nothing in her is being repaired. She has ninety years. Her parent has two hundred and fifty, and the parent is still alive and still does not need her.

And she is how the caverns keep the shape. Lanternfolk reproduce at the rate of a fungal symbiosis and the bloom took that with it. Ordinary human fertility and ordinary human gestation, roughly four times the parent's rate, is the only reason a lanternfolk-shaped body exists down here at all. She is not a rare specimen and she is not a curiosity. She is a reproductive strategy, and the strategy is her body, and it does not care what she has done with it.

That is the shape of her difficulty. The deadroad measure a life by how many of the realm's gates were already closed when you were born, and she is born into an unmeasurable one. Her subspecies carries no ceiling: the bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is structurally different from a colony and structurally unconstrained by it, so all three paths are open and nothing in the anatomy has ever refused her anything. There is no rung for her to arrive at and none to be refused by. She cannot be placed on the only scale her people have, and she cannot stop being a body that works.

So she has spent her cultivation running the sea outward instead of inward. The spirit-tier gate projects what is held in the sea out of the body as perception rather than as force, and it is the first rung on the ladder where a projected mind can meet anything at all. Every season she goes a little further out of herself than she comes back, because every season she is asked what the caverns will need next, and what they will need next is another one.

She is very clear. She is also, by her own arithmetic and by the arithmetic of her subspecies, spent.
history: Was born the first season after the colony strain failed, which is why nobody in the caverns has ever known a lanternfolk-shaped body that was not also a replacement one.
Grew up learning to see in a place where everything else in her family could already see, and was told early that this was a gift rather than a difference.
Was measured at the school that teaches by diffing laws and was entered as the control before she understood what the word meant.
Started taking the projection gate deliberately, after being asked what the caverns would need next and hearing the answer described in terms of her.
Worked out that the scale her people measure a life by cannot hold her kind at all, and decided that being unplaceable was cheaper than being placed and found wanting.

reference_stats.combat_read: Very hard to hurt for long and impossible to keep. She does not take a blow well because there is nothing in her that mends, but she does not go down either, and the cost of every second she is in a fight is a second off a frame that had no budget for it. The dangerous thing about her is not any of that: it is that an opponent who needs her to stop will not be able to, and an opponent who needs her to keep going can simply not stop.
reference_stats.notes: The species record states no ceiling for this subspecies, and that is an absence of obstruction rather than an absence of a ladder: the mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is why every path is open and why nothing in the body has ever refused anything. The record also attributes the loss of the parent species' longevity to the same replacement, and states that nothing in this body is repaired. No mechanical rule has been added here beyond what the species record states, and the subspecies' ordinary human fertility and gestation are the record's own explanation of how the shape survives at all.

canon.role_in_story: She is a brinecaller, which is a cross: a saltfolk spine with a tidecaller's chest seat, a body that metabolises brine and fresh water alike and so eats the pan and the tide without travelling between them to do it. It is the most portable body in the setting and its senses are the best chemical sense in the record, because it must tell two kinds of water apart at a glance and it is always being lied to by one of them. Its range bought it nothing on the ladder: the reservoir wall is inherited from the salt parent unchanged, and range is not power. What is rarely said out loud is that she has no kind. A brinecaller crosses freely in both directions and never produces a stable parent type, because the tolerance is a tolerance and not a plan, so her children are saltfolk and tidecallers and her siblings on whichever side of whichever shoreline are something else again. There is no brinecaller ancestor, no brinecaller line, and no brinecaller who has ever been taught anything by another brinecaller. The mind path is a discipline of transmission and its founding claim is that the self being cultivated can be separated from the one doing the cultivating, which has never once been tested by a body that cannot hand the practice to a second instance of itself. So she does the only thing available to a hybrid, which is to be the crossing: she runs the one unelemental circuit that cannot exist unless both halves are present, and she carries it from one shore to the other, because she is the only body that crosses a shoreline without a cut and she is never anywhere long enough to be the only one for long. She has never watched it continue.
canon.first_appearance: First seen walking up out of the shallows onto a stone apron with water still running off one side of her and not the other, handing a wrapped bundle to a shore-house keeper and telling her, before the keeper has asked, that whatever is inside it was done by somebody who is not the person who taught it to her.
canon.lore:
A brinecaller is a cross: a saltfolk spine with a tidecaller's chest seat, a body that metabolises brine and fresh water alike and therefore eats the pan and the tide without having to travel between them to do it. Its senses are the best chemical sense in the record, because it has to tell two kinds of water apart at a glance and it is always being lied to by one of them. It is the most portable body here and it inherited the salt parent's reservoir wall completely unchanged, which is the setting's standing reminder that range is not power.

What is not usually said out loud is that she has no kind. A brinecaller crosses freely in both directions and never produces a stable parent type, because the tolerance is a tolerance and not a plan. Her children are saltfolk and tidecallers. Her siblings are, on whichever side of whichever shoreline they were conceived, something else. There is no brinecaller ancestor, no brinecaller line, and no brinecaller who has ever been taught anything by another brinecaller.

The mind path is a discipline of transmission. That is not sentimentality; it is the ladder's own founding claim, that the self being cultivated can be separated from the one doing the cultivating, and no claim of that shape has ever been tested on a body that cannot put the practice into a second instance of itself. She is the only practitioner of her discipline on her ground who is also the only instance of her discipline on her ground.

So she does the only thing available to a hybrid, which is to be the crossing. The shared circuit runs one line from the reservoir up through the mind and back, so that each half feeds the other, and there is no elemental component in it at all, which means there is nothing to read and no matchup to anticipate. It also cannot be learned until both halves are at the floor, which is the closest thing her body has to a lineage. What it teaches her, and what no reading ever could, is that the point is the loop and not either end. She has carried it from one shoreline to the other more times than anybody could cite, because she is the only body here that crosses without a cut and a credential and a rite, and because a contested shoreline is the only ground she has ever been able to live on.

What she has never done is watch it continue. Every shore she reaches has somebody there carrying something that came out of her, and it is always a saltfolk or a tidecaller carrying it in one half of a circuit whose other half they cannot close.
history: Was conceived on one chemistry and carried on the other, and worked out early that this was normal for her and not an accident in her case.
Grew up moving between two shores with people who could each do half of what she could do and neither of whom could do all of it.
Learned to read both chemistries in a single pass and found, as everyone with her sense does, that one of them is permanently lying to her.
Taught the shared circuit to a household on the far shore and watched it arrive in a body that could not close the loop.
Stopped attempting to found a school of her own and began moving the practice itself instead, one shore at a time, without ever staying long enough to be its centre.

canon.role_in_story: She was not born and is not descended. She was sealed inside an authored object with a population that has been answering that object's resonance ever since, and the record's own note on how that population reproduces is the sentence she cannot get past: uncertain, probably not reproductive at all, and what looks like a population may be one very old thing wearing a great many faces. Every practitioner of her kind inside the seal is assumed to be one member of that population, including by the household that has been raising what an ascent leaves behind. She has no way to test the assumption from where she stands, because introspection on a body like hers is not private: her soul is seated along the resonance path rather than held in a frame, so a thing she half-remembers may be hers, may be the object's, or may be a face she has never worn that has somehow worn hers. She holds a memory of a childhood on a surface that is not the surface she is standing on. She is the longest-resident reader of the seal, which is a form of standing nobody can audit and nothing can inherit, because the conclusion lives in the object and the object is the only medium there is. And the mind path she is on is a ladder of separations: the fourth band asserts that the self being cultivated can be separated from the one doing the cultivating, and the spirit ascent asks whether a self can be held apart from a body at all. She is the worst-placed body in the setting for either question, and she is on a ladder that consists of nothing else.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing with her palm flat against a seam in the vault wall, not listening to it but matching it, and answering a register clerk's question about how long she had been resident by saying that the answer to that was a matter of whose face you were asking about.
canon.lore:
A vaultborn was sealed inside an authored object and has been answering that object's resonance ever since. Not descended and not born: the population is arranged along the object's inner surfaces, it takes its shape from whatever it stands on, and its qi comes from a single resonator distributed along a path through the thing. That is why the girdling and heel vessels come easily and the flank vessels do not, and why removing the object stops them. Nothing else in the setting is that completely non-portable.

The record's own note on reproduction is the sentence she cannot get past. It is uncertain, and probably not reproductive at all, and what looks like a population may be one very old thing wearing a great many faces.

She lives inside an object whose resonance is longer than any single life on the plains, and every practitioner of her kind inside it is assumed to be one member of a population. She has no way to test that assumption from where she stands. Introspection on a body like hers is not private, because the soul is seated along the resonance path rather than held in a frame: a thing she half-remembers may be hers, may be the object's, and may be a face she has never worn that has somehow worn hers. She has a memory of a childhood on a surface that is not the surface she is currently standing on, and there is no instrument in the setting that could tell her whether that is a childhood or a resonance.

The mind path is a ladder of separations. Its fourth band is where the setting asserts that the self being cultivated can be separated from the one doing the cultivating. The spirit ascent asks whether a self can be held apart from a body at all, which is a different and more expensive claim. She is the worst-placed body in the record for either question, and she is on a ladder that consists of them.

What she has instead of a lineage is duration. Nothing she concludes is inherited, because there is no line to inherit along. Nothing she concludes can be written outside the object and carried out, because the object is the only medium there is. The household that keeps what an ascent leaves behind has been raising faces for longer than most of them have been able to establish whether they are faces. She has been the longest-resident reader of the seal for most of a lifespan measured in the object's cycles, and she has never once been able to state, to anyone's satisfaction including her own, how many of her there are.
history: Came into being inside the vault with the population already in it, and has no account of a time before the resonance, because there is no time before the resonance.
Learned to hear the seal as a position rather than as a sound, which is the whole of her kind's navigation and the whole of her usefulness.
Took the mind path because it was the only discipline on the ladder that did not require leaving the object.
Formed a conclusion about the seal early, kept it, and has never been able to establish that it was hers to keep.
Began answering the household's questions about the seal's own record, and discovered that the answer to every one of them is the same answer, which nobody else can carry out.

personality.summary: A long-resident, absolutely still reader who has thought her way into a question she cannot answer and has not tried to make the question go away.
traits: answers a question about herself by first establishing whose question it is
will not repeat a reading, and gives the reason instead of the second number
is entirely honest about what she cannot tell and never softens it
takes an interest in people without any expectation of ever leaving the seal
treats doubt as a duty rather than as a symptom
mannerisms: puts a palm flat on the wall to match the seal before answering anything difficult
speaks with long pauses and does not fill them
refers to her own earlier statements as statements, without claiming them
turns to face a speaker by the position of the sound rather than by looking
stops mid-sentence to listen to the object, and resumes exactly where she was
motivations: to establish whether she is one practitioner or several, which is the only question she cannot answer
to get a conclusion about the seal out of the seal, in a form that will still mean something outside it
flaws: has spent so long inside one medium that she has stopped being able to imagine the question from outside it
cannot distinguish her own patience from the object's, and has not tried to
has let the household's need for answers become a substitute for an answer of her own
personality.voice: Slow, level, and precise. Uses long pauses that are listening rather than thinking, and has never once been observed to raise her voice.
taboos: will not give the same reading twice, even when asked for it twice
will not be entered in a register as a single practitioner, and has never once consented to it
will not leave the seal, on any ground, for any stated reason

reference_stats.summary: A vaultborn reader inside the object she was sealed in, whose discipline is a ladder of separations and whose own body cannot be shown to be one thing.
strengths: holds a contiguous record longer than any individual in the setting could, because the memory is the object's
hears the seal as a position, and navigates by it in total dark where nothing else can move
clears the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty
cannot be moved off her ground by anything short of removing the ground
weaknesses: has one pressure source, so the flank vessels are out of reach and the species stops there for arithmetic rather than for effort
cannot be carried anywhere, and stops entirely if the object is removed
cannot establish that a memory she holds is hers, which the ladder she is on is entirely about
her practice is a perturbation on the only instrument in the setting that could measure her
reference_stats.combat_read: Almost impossible to fight, because there is no portable part of her to fight with and no reserve to exhaust; and equally impossible to use, because anything done near the seal is something she has to hear. She is a resource with an address, and the address is the whole of her value and the whole of her problem.
reference_stats.notes: The authored ceiling for this species is the seventeenth gate and the authored mechanism is single-sourced: the flank vessels need two pressure sources held at once and a vaultborn has exactly one, the object's own resonance. The species record also states that reproduction is uncertain and probably not reproductive, which is the entire basis of this character's problem and is the record's own sentence rather than an addition. The ladder claims used here — that the cultivated self can be separated from the cultivator, and that a self may be held apart from a body — are the published descriptions of the fourth band and the spirit ascent.
